findings.claim: C9 returns the receipt timestamp as the age anchor without authenticating it against run.created_at or recomputing the pinned cron window. C3 does not compare these fields. Consequently a dispatch receipt can claim 2099 while independent REST says 2026, and a schedule receipt can claim a future/non-cron window or arbitrary cron, with no violations or warnings. This defeats the B2 freshness purpose and the no-refresh-on-rerun rule. Lexical date patterns also permit an impossible calendar date to be returned as a successful anchor. The positive schedule fixture is itself temporally impossible: receipt and every job start precede its run creation. The age threshold belongs to the consumer, but authenticity of its input must be defined before applying that threshold.

findings.claim: The numbered recipe both requires unconditional always() on steps 7-11 and asserts that failure of any step 1-6 means no receipt. The latter is not an invariant of that sequence: after a stamp/upload/setup/pip failure, REST, collection and receipt upload are still enabled. This is a specification contradiction, not evidence that a failed workflow becomes success.
